office_does: The three county commissioners are Pacific County's governing board: they adopt the budget, set land-use policy and fill vacancies in county offices. The District 3 (north county) seat is elected by all county voters.
race_blurb: Commission chair Jerry Doyle (Prefers Independent Party), elected in 2022 as a write-in primary candidate, faces Pacific County Republican Party chair Pattie Gray, who led him 750 to 600 in the District 3-only primary. Gray runs on lower taxes, cutting wasteful spending, term limits and less regulation; Doyle runs on balanced budgets and resisting state land-use rules.

candidates.summary: Chair of the Pacific County Republican Party and a paralegal, in her first run for county office, campaigning on lower taxes, spending cuts and limited government.
highlights: Supports "less taxation" and cutting "excessive regulations and red tape" [S1]
Would review every county department's budget "line by line" and audit departments regularly [S4][S3]
Wants term limits, a salary commission and commissioner pay cut to the county median income [S1][S3]
Would ease fees and permitting delays to make housing cheaper to build [S4]
Endorsed by the county Republican Party, Rep. Joel McEntire and Sen. Jeff Wilson [S2]

taxes.basis: Repeated explicit calls for less taxation and lower tax burdens in her statement and platform.

spending.basis: Stop 'wasteful spending', regular department audits, line-by-line budget review, live within means.

housing.basis: Affordability through cutting regulations, fees and permitting delays and pro-growth policies.

safety.basis: Platform: fully fund law enforcement and 'strong and real consequences for violence and theft'.

experience.basis: No government office held; her elected roles are party offices (precinct committee officer, state committeewoman, county chair).

reform.basis: Term limits, a lobbying ban for former officials, a salary commission and limits on executive sessions.

candidates.summary: Incumbent District 3 commissioner and commission chair, a general contractor, running on balanced budgets and resisting state land-use rules.
highlights: Says every budget he has worked on was balanced with core services preserved [S2]
Credits grants, fees and investment income for easing pressure on the general fund [S2]
Opposes added state regulation of land use under the Growth Management Act [S2][S6]
Says housing costs are driven by supply and demand and points to permitting reform [S2]
Led the board's August 2026 vote to recognize a deputy's medical retirement over the sheriff's objection [S7]

experience.basis: Four-year incumbent and board chair since 2024 running on his record.

spending.basis: Stresses balanced budgets and fiscal responsibility while preserving core services; no cut or expansion agenda.

housing.basis: Frames housing costs as supply and demand and points to permitting reform.

taxes.basis: Wants the state to 'control spending and not rely on us, the citizens, to bridge the gap'; no local tax pledge.
